results.content: What is reproducibility in measurement? Originally Answered: What term is used to describe the reproducibility of a measurement? Reproducibility in measurement describes the degree to which repeated measurements of the same quantity — made under changed conditions — yield consistent results. It is one of several precision concepts in metrology and quality science and answers the practical question: if different operators, instruments, times, or laboratories measure the same thing, how close will their results be? * Definition: Reproducibility = closeness of agreement between results obtained under changed conditions (different operators, equipment, laboratories, methods, or time).
